samples.summary: The four new numeric bands are applied only at the CRDT read boundaries; the paste sanitizer — the other untrusted producer — still admits unbounded values, so they reach layout un-banded and are persisted, then silently rewritten on the next reload
samples.evidence: `sanitizeInlineStyle` (clipboard.ts:141-145) takes `fontSize` through `asNumber`, which only requires `Number.isFinite` (clipboard.ts:69-71); `sanitizeBlockStyle` does the same for `lineHeight` (183-189), `sanitizeCellStyle` for `padding` (234-235), and `sanitizeImageData` for image `width`/`height` (110-115). `sanitizeTableData`'s `rowHeights` got a layout-side clamp in this diff (`table-layout.ts:253`) and the paginator got a per-row bound, but nothing bands a pasted `fontSize`/`lineHeight`/`padding`/image size at any sink. Consequences: (a) `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bounds pages *per row*, so a crafted payload with a 1000-row table whose cells carry `fontSize: 1e9` still asks for 200 pages × 1000 rows ≈ 200k `PageLine`s — a hang/OOM on paste, which is exactly the failure this diff exists to prevent; (b) even benignly, a pasted value outside the band renders in the live session, is written to the CRDT, and is then clamped (`fontSize`→400, `lineHeight`→20) or dropped entirely (an image whose edge exceeds `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE`, leaving the ￼ placeholder with no picture) the next time the document is read — the document changes under the user with no edit in between.
searchedFor: read table-layout.ts step 5b and pagination.ts row loop

samples.summary: `paginatableRowHeight` clips a legitimately tall table row's content out of both the screen and the PDF export, and desyncs `currentY` from `tl.rowYOffsets` for the rest of the table
samples.evidence: `return Math.min(raw, contentHeight * MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN)` caps the height the split loop consumes, but `tl.rowHeights[ri]` / `tl.rowYOffsets` are left unclamped. For a row whose *content* legitimately exceeds ~200 pages (a long document pasted into one cell — `computeTableLayout` steps 6-7 raise `rowHeights[curRow]` from content at table-layout.ts:293-294, so this is not only a poisoned attribute), everything past the bound emits no `PageLine` at all and is invisible in the canvas and in PDF export. Worse, `currentY` then advances by the clamped amount while later rows' `rowYOffsets` are unclamped, so `getTableOriginYForPageLine`'s `pageY + pl.y - rowYOffsets[lineIndex]` reconstructs a different table origin for the rows after it — their borders/backgrounds paint shifted. Silent truncation is the only terminating option for a poisoned height, but for content-derived height it is data the user can see disappear.

samples.summary: The bands are read-side only, so an import can persist an out-of-band value that renders one way now and differently after the next reload
samples.evidence: `normalizeFontSize` clamps to `MAX_FONT_SIZE = 400` and `normalizeLineHeight` to 20, applied only in `crdt-tree.ts`/`yorkie-doc-store.ts` on read. The DOCX importer writes `style.fontSize = halfPointsToPoints(parseInt(val, 10))` with no ceiling (`import/docx-style-map.ts:50`; Word permits `w:sz` up to 3276 half-points = 1638 pt) and `blockStyle.lineHeight = lineVal / 240` with no ceiling (`docx-style-map.ts:148`; under `lineRule="exact"` a large twips value yields a multiplier far above 20). Such a document renders at its imported size for the rest of the session and then silently at 400 pt / 20× after a reload. The module header's claim that "every band is the range the editor's own controls can reach, so nothing a gesture can produce is altered" does not cover the import sinks.

samples.summary: The new `lineHeight` band makes `parseBlockStyleAttrs`'s documented "the validator on the write side rejects exactly the values dropped here" false, so the v1 REST endpoint now accepts a value and silently rewrites it
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` validates every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry as "must be a finite number" only (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:399-407`), so `PUT ... style.lineHeight = 1e9` returns 200 and is stored; the reader added here clamps it to `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT` (20) on the way back out. The comment at crdt-attrs.ts:123-128 asserts the write-side validator rejects exactly what the reader drops, which no longer holds — an API caller's value is accepted and then quietly changed rather than 400'd.

samples.summary: `applyListLevelChanges` marks the wrong id dirty for a carried child that is missing from the layout-built parent map — the exact case `siblingBlocksOf`'s full-walk fallback was added for — so that child repaints at its old indent
samples.evidence: `const cellInfo = doc.blockParentMap.get(change.block.id); markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id);` — the map is only rebuilt by the layout pass, and the sibling lookup added in this diff deliberately resolves cell blocks that are absent from it. When the plan carries such a child, `cellInfo` is `undefined` and the *cell block's own id* goes into `dirtyBlockIds`. `recomputeLayout` passes that set to `computeLayout(doc.document.blocks, …, dirtyBlockIds, layoutCache)` (editor.ts:1523-1532), which keys on top-level block ids only, so the containing table is served from cache and the child keeps its stale lines — the very failure the accompanying comment says the `markDirty` prevents. `indent`/`outdent` only call `render()`, never `invalidateLayout()`, so nothing else recovers it.

samples.summary: `recordCursorForHistory()` now runs before the batch even when the gesture writes nothing, leaving a stale `pendingCursorPos` staged in `YorkieDocStore` for whatever mutation consumes it next
samples.evidence: `indent()`/`outdent()` (and `TextEditor.handleTab`/`handleIndent`/`handleOutdent`) call `recordCursorForHistory()` unconditionally; `YorkieDocStore.setCursorForHistory` sets `this.pendingCursorPos = pos` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3077) and only a subsequent write clears it via `consumePendingCursor`. When the plan is empty — Cmd+] on a subtree already at `MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, Shift+Tab at level 0, or a caret on a non-list block — no write happens, so the pre-gesture caret stays staged and the next mutation that does not refresh it first would record a stale caret as its undo target (the #523 class of defect). The old `indent()` called `docStore.snapshot()` only and never staged a cursor, so this is new; impact is limited because ordinary edits re-stage through `saveSnapshot`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the four bands in model/numeric-attrs.ts are imported only by crdt-tree.ts:43-45, yorkie-doc-store.ts:52-54 and crdt-attrs.ts:149 (lineHeight); no other importer exists anywhere in packages/**. clipboard.ts's asNumber (69-71) checks only Number.isFinite, and sanitizeInlineStyle (141-145), sanitizeBlockStyle (183-189), sanitizeCellStyle (234-235) and sanitizeImageData (110-116) pass fontSize/lineHeight/padding/image size through it unbanded. The paste path (text-editor.ts:1685 -> insertBlocks 4248-4352 -> yorkie-doc-store.ts:2146-2171) both serializes those raw values into the Yorkie tree (serializeInlineStyle lines 135, 146-152) and splices the raw Block objects into this.cachedDoc with dirty=false, so layout consumes them un-banded in the live session while the next read through parseInlineStyle (199-202) / parseCellStyle (322-325) clamps or drops them — a real live-vs-reload divergence. The only downstream bounds are narrower than the exposure: table-layout.ts:251-258 normalizes only stored rowHeights, not the content-derived cellHeight (189-196) or lineHeight (layout.ts:874-885), and pagination.ts:79-83 bounds pages per row only, with the fragment loop at 161-190 running per row. No counterexample found.
